InitialDescription: Gentle and clean. It opens with steady handling but becomes hot and scorched if pushed too hard or too long.
Carries light bitterness and sweet return. If handled too aggressively, bitterness rushes out before sweetness.
Rich and deep, useful as a leading note or tail note. If it takes too much space, it becomes bitter and dominant.
Mild and smooth. It gives body and texture, but it can blur stronger aromas if it takes the lead.
Solid and warm. It gives a biscuit-like nut aroma and blends well with similar nutty ingredients.
Thick and warm. It is good at building a base before lighter notes appear.
Bright and slightly bitter. It lifts the middle or finish, but becomes bitter if it arrives too early or too strongly.
Clean and mild. It rounds the finish and can cover detail if it leads too early.
Deep, dry, and aromatic. It needs enough pressure to open, but excessive pressure turns it harsh.
A support ingredient. It strengthens the base but should not become the main aroma.
Clear and piercing. It needs a controlled release; rushing it makes the spice harsh.
Light and fragile. It works as a fresh wrapper note and can be crushed by early, heavy, or excessive handling.
Savory and fermented. It carries body, but rough handling can make it dull, bitter, or muddy.
Fresh and sharp. It opens brightness, but can rush forward and dominate if handled too aggressively.
Fresh and watery. It keeps a clean finish, but heavy or early handling can bury its freshness.
